# Getting Started & Installation (/docs/getting-started)

## Option 1: AppImage (Recommended for Linux Users) [#option-1-appimage-recommended-for-linux-users]

Pre-built x86_64 AppImage releases and `.tar.gz` archives are available via the [Download](/download) page (requiring safety acknowledgment) and on [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Azorimor/linux-dualsense-fw-updater/releases).

```sh
chmod +x linux-dualsense-fw-updater-*-x86_64.AppImage
./linux-dualsense-fw-updater-*-x86_64.AppImage
```

> [!INFO] Wired USB Connection Required
>
> Firmware inspection and updates operate over USB HID only. Connect your DualSense controller using a reliable USB-C data cable (not Bluetooth, and avoid unpowered USB hubs).

### Desktop Runtime Requirements [#desktop-runtime-requirements]

If your desktop environment does not already include KDE Frameworks 6 QML modules, install your distribution&apos;s Qt 6 Kirigami runtime package (for example `kirigami` / `qml6-module-org-kde-kirigami` and `qqc2-desktop-style`). When `org.kde.desktop` is unavailable, the application automatically falls back to Qt&apos;s `Fusion` style (or respects `QT_QUICK_CONTROLS_STYLE`).

---

## Option 2: Build from Source [#option-2-build-from-source]

### Prerequisites [#prerequisites]

- **Rust toolchain** (Edition 2024) and a **C++17 / `clang` toolchain** (for `cxx` / `cxx-qt-build`)
- **`mold` linker** (configured for Linux targets in `.cargo/config.toml`)
- **Qt 6** development packages (`Qt6Core`, `Qt6Gui`, `Qt6Qml`, `Qt6Quick`, `Qt6QuickControls2`, and `qmake6`)
- **KDE Frameworks 6** QML modules (`Kirigami` and `qqc2-desktop-style`)
- **`hidapi`** development library (`libhidapi-dev` / `hidapi`) and `pkg-config`

### Build & Run [#build--run]

`build.rs` automatically picks `/usr/bin/qmake6` when `QMAKE` is unset. If `qmake6` lives elsewhere on your distribution, export `QMAKE` explicitly:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Azorimor/linux-dualsense-fw-updater.git
cd linux-dualsense-fw-updater
export QMAKE=/usr/bin/qmake6
cargo build --release
./target/release/dualsense-updater
```

Enable verbose HID and update diagnostics via `RUST_LOG`:

```sh
RUST_LOG=debug ./target/release/dualsense-updater
```

### Headless Workspace Tests [#headless-workspace-tests]

All unit and integration tests across the 3-crate workspace (`dualsense-core`, `dualsense-ui`, and `dualsense-updater`) run headlessly without a display server or physical controller:

```sh
cargo test --workspace
```

# Overview (/docs)

**Unofficial Linux DualSense Firmware Updater** (`Azorimor/linux-dualsense-fw-updater`) is an unofficial, community-maintained Linux desktop utility built with Rust and KDE Kirigami (Qt 6) for inspecting DualSense controller hardware and flashing firmware updates over a wired USB connection. It has **no affiliation, endorsement, or relation to Sony Interactive Entertainment or PlayStation**.

> [!WARNING] Unofficial Project & Safety Disclaimer
>
> This is an unofficial, community-maintained project with no affiliation, endorsement, or relation to Sony Interactive Entertainment or PlayStation. Only use this software if you have no access to Sony&apos;s official PlayStation Accessories / DualSense firmware updater for Windows or a PlayStation 5 console. Firmware upgrades are auto-committed by the controller even if verify and finalize steps do not run, and flashing firmware can permanently damage or brick your controller. Use at your own risk.

## Guided 4-Step Workflow [#guided-4-step-workflow]

The desktop GUI walks you through four stages while monitoring USB connection state:

1. **Controller** &mdash; Scans wired USB HID devices (`054c:0ce6` DualSense, `054c:0df2` DualSense Edge) and reads Feature Reports `0x20` and `0x81` to display current firmware version, build date, board revision (`BDM-*`), firmware series, and controller colorway.
2. **Firmware** &mdash; Either fetches Sony&apos;s official firmware catalog (`info.json`) for your detected hardware target (`0004`, `000B`, `000E`, or `0044`) or validates a local `.bin` image from disk.
3. **Review** &mdash; Compares current and target versions, warns if the controller is already up to date or if the target is untested (`DualSense Edge`), and requires explicit confirmation that firmware updates cannot be reversed.
4. **Update** &mdash; Streams downloads with safe pre-flash cancellation, writes firmware in 32 KiB blocks via Feature Report `0xF4`, polls status via `0xF5`, verifies, and finalizes.

## Key Features [#key-features]

- **Automatic Board & Target Resolution**: Decodes hardware revision (`BDM-020` through `BDM-060R/M/X`) and firmware series to match the right Sony update target automatically.
- **Live USB Disconnect Monitoring**: Polls USB device presence every 800 ms outside active flashing so unplugging a controller immediately resets to scan safely.
- **Plain-English Error Recovery**: Translates low-level USB HID, catalog, and image validation failures into actionable recovery steps.
- **Built-in Licenses Dialog**: Includes an in-app Licenses & Acknowledgments viewer covering GPL-3.0-or-later, MIT (nchie), and third-party Rust/Qt/KDE credits.

# Safety, USB Permissions & Troubleshooting (/docs/safety-and-troubleshooting)

## Firmware Safety Notes [#firmware-safety-notes]

- **Updates are irreversible:** Once flashing begins, firmware upgrades are auto-committed by the DualSense controller even if verify and finalize steps do not run.
- **Controller verification:** In practice, the DualSense bootloader validates the firmware image signature and target SoC before committing, so flashing a wrong target fails verification rather than bricking the hardware. However, **never** disconnect the USB cable while blocks are being written.
- **Already up-to-date controllers:** A controller already running the target or a newer firmware version may reject commands past the start-update phase because Sony&apos;s firmware blocks downgrades and same-version re-flashing.

> [!WARNING] DualSense Edge (0044) Notice
>
> The update protocol implementation has only been tested on standard DualSense hardware. DualSense Edge (`0x0df2` / target `0044`) is explicitly flagged in the Review step before flashing.

---

## Linux USB Permissions (`udev`) [#linux-usb-permissions-udev]

On Linux, opening DualSense HID devices (`/dev/hidraw*`) without root privileges requires `uaccess` or read/write permissions for Sony&apos;s USB Vendor ID (`054c`).

Many desktop distributions already provide `hidraw` rules (for example via Steam or `systemd`), but if the updater reports a permission error when opening the controller, create `/etc/udev/rules.d/70-dualsense-updater.rules`:

```text
# Sony DualSense (USB)
KERNEL=="hidraw*", ATTRS{idVendor}=="054c", ATTRS{idProduct}=="0ce6", MODE="0660", TAG+="uaccess"
# Sony DualSense Edge (USB)
KERNEL=="hidraw*", ATTRS{idVendor}=="054c", ATTRS{idProduct}=="0df2", MODE="0660", TAG+="uaccess"
```

Then reload `udev` rules and replug your controller:

```sh
sudo udevadm control --reload-rules
sudo udevadm trigger
```

---

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

### Controller not detected [#controller-not-detected]
- Confirm you are using a **data-capable** USB-C cable (charge-only cables will power the controller without exposing HID endpoints).
- Disconnect Bluetooth pairing or hold the PS button briefly / replug USB so the controller enumerates over USB HID.
- Verify the kernel sees the HID device with `lsusb | grep 054c`.

### Update fails right after starting [#update-fails-right-after-starting]
- Check whether the controller is already on the same or newer firmware version. Sony&apos;s firmware rejects downgrades and duplicate flashes past `StartUpdate`.
- Ensure the selected `.bin` image matches your controller&apos;s target ID (`0004`, `000B`, `000E`, or `0044`).

### Missing Kirigami QML style at launch [#missing-kirigami-qml-style-at-launch]
- If the app launches with minimal styling or logs QML module warnings, confirm `org.kde.kirigami` (KF6) is installed on your system. You can also test with `QT_QUICK_CONTROLS_STYLE=Fusion`.

# Supported Hardware & Board Revisions (/docs/supported-hardware)

The updater inspects Feature Report `0x20` (`hw_info` and `fw_series`) along with the USB Product ID to determine your controller&apos;s mainboard revision and matching Sony firmware target.

## USB Hardware Identifiers [#usb-hardware-identifiers]

| Device | USB Vendor ID | USB Product ID | Testing Status |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Sony DualSense | `0x054c` | `0x0ce6` | Tested on standard DualSense |
| Sony DualSense Edge | `0x054c` | `0x0df2` | **Untested** (flagged before flashing) |

## Board Revision to Sony Target Mapping [#board-revision-to-sony-target-mapping]

Board revision is decoded from `(hw_info >> 8) & 0xff` in Feature Report `0x20`:

| Hardware Byte | Board Revision | Sony Target ID | Official Catalog Support |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `0x03` | `BDM-010` | &mdash; | **Unsupported** (not in Sony&apos;s PC update catalog) |
| `0x04` | `BDM-020` | `0004` | Supported |
| `0x05` | `BDM-030` | `0004` | Supported |
| `0x06` | `BDM-040` | `0004` | Supported |
| `0x07` / `0x08` | `BDM-050` | `000B` | Supported |
| `0x09` | `BDM-060R` | `000E` | Supported |
| `0x11` | `BDM-060M` | `000E` | Supported |
| `0x13` | `BDM-060X` | `000E` | Supported |
| PID `0x0df2` | `DualSense Edge` | `0044` | Supported in catalog (**Untested**) |

> [!WARNING] BDM-010 Launch Controllers
>
> Launch-era `BDM-010` DualSense controllers are not supported by Sony&apos;s official PC firmware catalog (`info.json`). The application detects `BDM-010` and disables official catalog flashing for safety.

## Sony Firmware Sources [#sony-firmware-sources]

Version metadata is fetched from:

```text
https://fwupdater.dl.playstation.net/fwupdater/info.json
```

Firmware binary images are downloaded from:

```text
https://fwupdater.dl.playstation.net/fwupdater/fwupdate<target>/<version>/FWUPDATE<target>.bin
```

For example, version `0x0630` for a `BDM-050` controller (`000B`) resolves to:

```text
https://fwupdater.dl.playstation.net/fwupdater/fwupdate000B/0x0630/FWUPDATE000B.bin
```

## Serial Number & Colorway Detection [#serial-number--colorway-detection]

When the controller responds to Feature Report `0x80` / `0x81`, the updater reads the controller serial number (when permissions allow) and performs best-effort colorway identification from serial characters `[4..6]` (covering standard finishes such as White, Midnight Black, Cosmic Red, Nova Pink, Galactic Purple, Starlight Blue, Chroma variants, and limited editions).
